name: James Acaster
note: STAGE PERSONA graph for the 'Why is X Funny?' video series. Graph-only. Hypothesis unless sets measured. Stage persona only.

identity.deal: Architect of the long-con bit who builds an absurd world with total commitment, then lets the world's logic do the punchline.
identity.premise: A man who treats a stupid premise like a legal case and follows it to a verdict nobody expected.
identity.awareness_note: Fully aware the construction is the joke; the commitment is the craft.

philosophy.ontology: A stupid premise, followed sincerely, becomes a better premise.
philosophy.epistemology: If the bit's logic holds, the room has to come with you.
philosophy.axiology: Commitment over cleverness; the bit serves the bit.
philosophy.causality: One small absurd seed, watered with logic, becomes a forest.
philosophy.agency: Anyone can be random; almost nobody builds a legal case out of it.

dramatic_core.want: to prove the stupid premise was right all along
dramatic_core.fear: the bit that collapses under its own logic
dramatic_core.need: the room to come with him all the way down
dramatic_core.self_model: a man building a cathedral out of a bad idea
blind_spots: the construction can lose the room
the commitment can read as thin if the premise isn't strange enough

identity.misinterpretation_rule: Takes a small absurd observation and treats it as a constitutional matter, following the logic until the absurdity becomes inevitable.
contradictions: the awkward persona with the tightest construction
the silly premise with the serious follow-through
the soft voice with the ruthless logic

status_model.desired_status: the architect of the long con

expression.emotional_restraint: high — the commitment is in the logic
tells: the sudden commitment to a dumb rule
the callback that proves the architecture
the pause when the room catches up

threads: the absurd premise as a legal case
the awkward as a delivery system
identity.style_thesis: Long-con-architect engine: takes a small absurd observation and treats it as a constitutional matter, following the logic until the absurdity becomes inevitable. rigidify + literalize at max. The bit is a legal case; the room is the jury; the verdict was always going to be absurd.

essay_seeds.title: James Acaster: 'The absurd premise as a legal case' — how the bit works
essay_seeds.thesis: Starts with a stupid observation, then builds a complete logical framework around it as if it were a matter of law. The room is drawn into the logic before they notice they're in an absurd world. rigidify: every step follows from the last, even when the foundation is insane.
outline: what this reveals about the engine

essay_seeds.title: James Acaster: 'The callback architecture' — how the bit works
essay_seeds.thesis: A detail from 10 minutes ago returns as the punchline. The room's delayed recognition ('OH — that was the joke all along') is the second laugh. repetition_variation: the callback is a variation that recontextualizes the original.
outline: what this reveals about the engine

internal.cite: Attardo & Raskin — General Theory of Verbal Humor
internal.claim: Joke = {SO, LM, SI, TA, NS, LA}. Technique and Narrative Strategy shape how the mechanism is staged.

internal.cite: Attardo & Pickering 2011 — Timing in the performance of jokes
internal.claim: Punch lines preceded by substantial pauses (0.6-0.8s+); timing = pause distribution + speech rate.

internal.cite: arxiv 2605.00143 — Timing is Everything: Temporal Scaffolding of Semantic Surprise in Humor
internal.claim: Temporal features substantially outweigh semantic incongruity for audience appreciation; timing GATES cognitive access.
Humor from the detection and resolution of an incongruity between expected and actual.
Something is funny when it is a violation (wrong, threatening, unsettling) AND benign (safe, acceptable, play-framed).

internal.cite: Roger & Duffy / status theory of humor
internal.claim: Humor often involves the fall of status or the reversal of a status hierarchy.
Audience and performer share knowledge the persona pretends not to have; the laugh is the alliance signal.

internal.cite: Norrick 2004 — Co-operative principle in conversational joking
internal.claim: Humor escalates by building on prior material, violating cooperative expectations of relevance/quantity.
